site.name: larkfit-mobile
site.summary: larkfit-mobile Fictional fitness tracker "Lark" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Workouts / Activity / You - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full larkfit-mobile system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Lark mobile web application successfully implements basic tab navigation and a clean layout structure, but it currently suffers from significant interaction and usability gaps. Primary issues include consistently undersized touch targets across filtering and navigation controls, a lack of empty states for zero-result searches, and broken scrolling that hides critical profile actions on mobile devices. Additionally, numerous high-visibility call-to-actions are implemented as non-functional stubs, blocking core user flows.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full larkfit-mobile system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will systematically test the single-page application by navigating through the four main bottom tabs (Today, Workouts, Activity, You). It will interact with actionable elements on each screen, such as workout play buttons and profile inputs. Finally, it will verify layout constraints and touch target sizes, especially considering the mobile-first design.
assumptions: The application is a single HTML file (index.html) that uses JavaScript to switch between screens based on the bottom tab bar clicks.
The 2 inputs mentioned in the prescan are located within the 'You' (profile/settings) tab.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (e.g., the '+' button and '▶' play buttons) that trigger layout warnings
Visibility and stickiness of the bottom 4-tab navigation bar during scrolling
Scrolling behavior within the simulated mobile frame on desktop vs. native edge-to-edge on mobile

phases.title: Bottom Tab Navigation Validation
phases.objective: Verify that all four bottom tabs correctly switch the visible screen content.
key_checks: Click '▶ Workouts', '📊 Activity', and '◉ You' tabs sequentially
Verify headings change (e.g., 'Workouts', 'Activity', 'You') to confirm screen transitions
exit_criteria: All four tabs have been clicked and their corresponding main headings are confirmed visible.

phases.title: Today Screen Interactions
phases.objective: Explore actionable elements on the default 'Today' dashboard.
key_checks: Click the '+' button at the top
Click the '▶' play button next to 'Easy 5K' or 'Hip-mobility flow'
Check if a modal, workout active state, or new view appears
exit_criteria: Primary action buttons on the Today screen have been triggered and state changes recorded.

phases.title: Workouts and Activity Exploration
phases.objective: Investigate content and interactions within the Workouts and Activity screens.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Workouts', click on a workout card (e.g., 'Easy 5K · recovery') to check for detail views
Navigate to 'Activity', look for interactive charts, 'Recent' logs, or '30-day intensity' filters
exit_criteria: Both screens have been scrolled and any visible interactive lists or charts tested.

phases.title: Profile and Settings (You Tab)
phases.objective: Test form inputs and preference toggles on the user profile screen.
key_checks: Identify and interact with the 2 inputs found in the prescan
exit_criteria: Inputs have been focused/modified and settings toggles clicked.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit index.html and trigger all 4 main virtual screens via the tab bar.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise workout playback buttons, quick add (+), tab navigation, and settings inputs.
coverage_targets.mobile: Ensure the UI functions correctly in a mobile viewport, paying attention to the bottom bar and tap targets.

notes: Since this is a mobile fixture, be mindful of scrolling within specific elements if the main body does not scroll.
Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets (< 44px) when evaluating UX.

findings.user_goal: Interact with buttons and filters accurately on a mobile touch screen.
findings.problem: Numerous interactive elements have tap targets that are too small for comfortable touch interaction.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and trajectory logs indicate that category filter chips (All, Run, Bike, etc.) are only 29px high. Additionally, the settings (⚙), add (+), back (←), and action (⤴) top bar icons range from 34px to 38px, and the 'Adjust goals' button is 33px high.
findings.why_it_matters: Touch targets below the standard 44x44px minimum lead to user frustration, misclicks, and a feeling that the app is unpolished or difficult to use on mobile devices.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height/width of all clickable icons, filter chips, and inline buttons to at least 44x44px to ensure mobile accessibility standards are met.

findings.user_goal: Perform core actions like starting a workout, editing preferences, or adding a new activity.
findings.problem: Several prominent call-to-action buttons act as dead ends, providing no feedback or state change when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Start workout', 'Adjust goals', 'Sign out', '+', '⚙', and '⤴' buttons produces no visible changes, modals, or URL updates.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on these primary buttons to achieve their goals within the app. Dead buttons break trust and completely block the user from using the core functionality they expect from a fitness tracker.
findings.suggestion: Implement the functional pathways for these buttons, or if they are placeholders, display a 'Coming Soon' toast notification to acknowledge the user's tap and provide system feedback.

findings.user_goal: Scroll to view all content on a screen, particularly settings and profile information.
findings.problem: Scrolling is broken or improperly configured on the 'You' (profile) screen, preventing access to bottom-anchored content.
findings.evidence: In the mobile viewport, standard scrolling and dragging failed to move the viewport on the 'You' screen, leaving the 'PREFERENCES' section and the 'Sign out' button permanently hidden off-screen (y=1018).
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot scroll, they are completely locked out of accessing their account settings, preferences, and the ability to log out, rendering that portion of the app useless on smaller devices.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the main content container for tabs has `overflow-y: auto` properly applied, and verify that touch events are not being unintentionally swallowed by a parent container.
findings.source_hint: The container holding the 'You' tab content.

findings.user_goal: Understand when a search or filter yields no results.
findings.problem: Combining searches and filters that result in zero matches leaves a completely blank screen without explanation.
findings.evidence: When searching for 'run' and clicking the 'Bike' filter, the list correctly filters to zero items, but the UI displays a blank white area below the filters with no text or graphic.
findings.why_it_matters: A blank screen can be interpreted as the app freezing, failing to load, or breaking. Explicit feedback is required to tell the user that their specific query returned no results.
findings.suggestion: Implement an explicit empty state component (e.g., 'No workouts found matching [search term]') when the filtered list array is empty.
findings.source_hint: The workouts list container on index.html

findings.user_goal: Filter activity data by different time periods to track progress.
findings.problem: The time filter dropdown on the Activity screen does not actually update the displayed metrics.
findings.evidence: Changing the time filter dropdown from 'Last 30 days' to 'This week' does not dynamically update the metric values (workouts, time, distance, cal), which remain static.
findings.why_it_matters: If a filter appears to work visually but the underlying data does not change, users may mistakenly believe they have achieved different results, ultimately leading to a loss of trust in the app's data accuracy.
findings.suggestion: Wire the select dropdown's `onChange` event to properly trigger a state update that recalculates and re-renders the dashboard metrics for the selected timeframe.

findings.user_goal: Understand the purpose of a dropdown menu using a screen reader.
findings.problem: The time filter dropdown menu lacks an accessible name.
findings.evidence: The `<select>` element for the time filter on the Activity screen triggers a warning for missing a label or `aria-label`.
findings.why_it_matters: Without an accessible name, users relying on assistive technologies will hear that it is a dropdown menu but will not know what data it controls (e.g., 'Timeframe').
findings.suggestion: Add an `aria-label="Select time period"` to the `<select>` element, or associate it with a visible `<label>` using the `for` attribute.
findings.source_hint: select dropdown on the Activity screen
